text: If there is one word that you find coming out like a bomb from the Upanishads, bursting like a bomb-shell upon masses of ignorance, it is the word fearlessness.
source: Swami Vivekananda, The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Complete Works, Vol. 3, 3.4 Lectures From Colombo to Almora → 3.4.6 Reply to the Address of Welcome at Paramakudi, Advaita Ashrama.

text: A man must go about his duties without taking notice of the sneers and the ridicule of the world.
source: Swami Vivekananda, The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Complete Works, Vol. 1, 1.2 Karma-Yoga → 1.2.2 Chapter 2: Each Is Great in His Own Place, Advaita Ashrama.

text: All power is within you; you can do anything and everything.
source: Swami Vivekananda, The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Complete Works, Vol. 3, 3.4 Lectures From Colombo to Almora → 3.4.14 The Work Before Us, Advaita Ashrama.

text: You cannot believe in God until you believe in yourself.
source: Swami Vivekananda, The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Complete Works, Vol. 5, 5.6 Sayings and Utterances, Advaita Ashrama.

text: To me the very essence of education is concentration of mind, not the collecting of facts.
source: Swami Vivekananda, The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Complete Works, Vol. 6, 6.1 Lectures and Discourses → 6.1.5 Concentration and Breathing, Advaita Ashrama.

text: How has all the knowledge in the world been gained but by the concentration of the powers of the mind?
source: Swami Vivekananda, The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Complete Works, Vol. 1, 1.3 Raja-Yoga → 1.3.1 Chapter 1: Introductory, Advaita Ashrama.

text: Make that one idea your life — think of it, dream of it, live on that idea.
source: Swami Vivekananda, The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Complete Works, Vol. 1, 1.3 Raja-Yoga → 1.3.6 Chapter 6: Pratyahara and Dharana, Advaita Ashrama.

text: Awake, arise, and stop not till the goal is reached!
source: Swami Vivekananda, The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Complete Works, Vol. 1, 1.4 Lectures and Discourses → 1.4.16 The Gita Iii, Advaita Ashrama.

text: Never mind failures; they are quite natural, they are the beauty of life, these failures.
source: Swami Vivekananda, The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Complete Works, Vol. 2, 2.5 Jnana-Yoga → 2.5.7 Chapter 7: God in Everything, Advaita Ashrama.

text: Purity, patience, and perseverance are the three essentials to success and, above all, love.
source: Swami Vivekananda, The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Complete Works, Vol. 6, 6.4 Epistles – Second Series → 6.4.51 Nanjunda Rao, Advaita Ashrama.

text: Strength is life, weakness is death.
source: Swami Vivekananda, The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Complete Works, Vol. 5, 5.5 Conversations and Dialogues → 5.5.2 Shri Surendra Nath Sen, Advaita Ashrama.

text: Anything that makes you weak physically, intellectually, and spiritually, reject as poison; there is no life in it, it cannot be true.
source: Swami Vivekananda, The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Complete Works, Vol. 3, 3.4 Lectures From Colombo to Almora → 3.4.11 My Plan of Campaign, Advaita Ashrama.

text: Therefore it is necessary that Kriya-yoga should be constantly practised, in order to gain control of the mind, and bring it into subjection.
source: Swami Vivekananda, The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Complete Works, Vol. 1, 1.3 Raja-Yoga → 1.3.9.2 Concentration: Its Practice, Advaita Ashrama.

text: Take the whole responsibility on your own shoulders, and know that you are the creator of your own destiny.
source: Swami Vivekananda, The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Complete Works, Vol. 2, 2.5 Jnana-Yoga → 2.5.11b Chapter 11b: The Cosmos, Advaita Ashrama.

text: They alone live who live for others, the rest are more dead than alive.
source: Swami Vivekananda, The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Complete Works, Vol. 4, 4.3 Writings: Prose → 4.3.14 Our Duty to the Masses, Advaita Ashrama.

text: Where should you go to seek for God — are not all the poor, the miserable, the weak, Gods? Why not worship them first?
source: Swami Vivekananda, The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Complete Works, Vol. 5, 5.1 Epistles First Series → 5.1.21 Alasinga, Advaita Ashrama.
